Alignment settling

Where the axis ends up after coils A and C are cut, and how long until it stays there. Campaign 2026-09-09/10, 107 repeats, solved every frame.

71 of 107 repeats settle. The settling time rises with drive, from 1.22 s at 30 Hz to 2.41 s at 110 Hz.

What this does not settle

  • 36 of 107 repeats do not settle inside the 5 s window. Mostly because the trace still wanders wider than the band where it is supposed to have arrived. Whether that is the robot or the rig is not established here; finding out means a longer DROP_MS, which costs coil heat at exactly the frequencies where heat is already the binding constraint.
  • The rise time is unavailable wherever the rise is short. The reported values sit against a 0.25 s smoother, so the faster ones carry about 10% of filter. A rise shorter than the smoother is refused rather than reported as the filter's own width.
  • The cone sitting at 1.00× the drive does not prove the rotor spins at the drive. The field itself rotates at that rate and can shake the robot whatever the rotor is doing. What it establishes is where the line is, which is all the filter needs to know.
  • The coning settling time carries the band's frequency dependence. It is 10% of an excursion that itself grows with drive, so it drifts downward with frequency for reasons that are not the robot (25.12). The decay constant τ is band-free and flat; quote that instead.
  • This is coning, not precession, and the two are different modes. The wobble measured here sits at 1.00× the drive frequency at every frequency from 20 to 100 Hz, which is the signature of a body-fixed asymmetry carried round by the rotor. §11.3's free precession is a separate mode at a roughly constant ~1.2 Hz, and the 2–4 Hz line removed from these traces is a third thing again — mechanical, tracking neither. This campaign has isolated the first and not the other two.
  • The coning decay constant is not converted to a damping coefficient. It is fitted and it is flat across the sweep, which is what a dissipation-limited mode should do — but τ is the decay of an RMS envelope and §11.3's ct multiplies a rate in a complex tilt variable. The factor between them is not derived.
  • 40 Hz mixes two hold times and shows as two populations — two traces at 49° of swing against twelve at 11.5°. The median is quoted over both and should not be.
